description: field/hit `[a-é]+` (cls-boundary-range): 'café' -- every character (c,a,f,é) is in the range U+0061..U+00E9
field/hit `[\x{100}-\x{2000}]+` (cls-high-range): a Cyrillic word, entirely inside the range
field/miss `[^é]` (cls-neg-single): the WHOLE subject is é alone -- no non-é character exists to match

field/edge, THREE members at once: `[^\x{80}-\x{10FFFF}]+` (cls-neg-allhigh) MISSES (no ASCII byte anywhere); `\w+` without UCP (cls-w-ascii) MISSES (Cyrillic letters are not ASCII word chars); `(*UCP)\w+` (cls-w-ucp) HITS on the same text
field/hit `[a-zé\x{430}-\x{44F}]+` (cls-mixed) AND `[^\x{4E00}-\x{9FFF}]+` (cls-neg-cjk, none of these characters is Han): a, é, б in one run
field/hit `.` (cls-dot): one CJK character
field/hit `^.{5}$` (cls-dot-rep): 5 CHARACTERS (4x 2-byte + 1x 4-byte) totalling 12 BYTES
field/miss `^.{5}$` (cls-dot-rep): 3 characters (1+2+2 bytes = 5 BYTES) -- 5 bytes but only 3 characters, so it must NOT match
field/hit `\w+` ascii-scoped (cls-w-ascii) and `[[:alpha:]]+` (cls-posix-alpha): plain ASCII
field/edge, digit ascii/ucp PAIR: four Arabic-Indic digits -- `\d{4}` ascii-scoped (cls-d-ascii) MISSES, `(*UCP)\d{4}` (cls-d-ucp) HITS
field/edge, space ascii/ucp PAIR: 'a' NBSP 'b' -- `a\sb` ascii-scoped (cls-s-nbsp) MISSES, `(*UCP)a\sb` (cls-s-ucp) HITS
field/edge `[[:alpha:]]+` (cls-posix-alpha): 'Straße' -- the ASCII-scoped run stops at ß (not an ASCII letter), a scope-boundary witness
field/hit `[α-ω]+` (cls-lead-pair): Greek alpha-beta-gamma, a class UD 6.3 says a two-lead-byte bitmap-skip arm must take
field/miss `[^\x{4E00}-\x{9FFF}]+` (cls-neg-cjk): pure Han text -- every character IS in the negated range, so no run can match
field/hit `[^\x{80}-\x{10FFFF}]+` (cls-neg-allhigh): pure byte-clean ASCII
field/hit `é` (lit-1ch-2b): one 2-byte character alone
field/hit `日` (lit-1ch-3b): one 3-byte character alone
field/hit `😀` (lit-1ch-4b): one 4-byte character alone
field/hit `日本語` (lit-run-3) AND `^日本語$` (lit-anchored-run): the EXACT 9-byte run, nothing else
field/near-miss `日本語` (lit-nearmiss-run's own twin): shares two characters (six bytes) and fails at the third
field/hit `user@例え.jp` (lit-mixed-ascii): the exact mixed-width literal, ASCII @ and . available as the necessary byte
field/miss `user@例え.jp` (lit-mixed-ascii): the @ is replaced, breaking the literal
field/hit `Москва` (lit-cyr-run): the exact 12-byte run, every lead byte 0xD0/0xD1
field/hit `é@` (lit-offset-at-tail): THE FIRST CUSTOMER (P1) -- the necessary byte at the TAIL
field/hit `@é` (lit-offset-at-head): P1's order pair -- the necessary byte at the HEAD
field/miss `café` PRECOMPOSED (lit-nfc-pair): a DECOMPOSED subject (e + COMBINING ACUTE, U+0301) -- byte-different from the precomposed pattern, no normalization happens anywhere on this roster
field/hit `café` PRECOMPOSED (lit-nfc-pair): the precomposed form, embedded in a sentence
field/hit `Straße` (lit-sharp-s): the exact literal with its 2-byte ß, embedded
field/miss `Straße` (lit-sharp-s): case-sensitive AND 'SS' != 'ß' -- neither substitution matches the literal
field/edge `^日本語$` (lit-anchored-run): the run plus trailing content -- lit-run-3 still HITS (substring search) but the anchored form MISSES (extra suffix breaks the exact match)

field/edge, THREE members at once: `(?i)é` (ci-e-acute) HITS on uppercase É; `(*UCP)(?i)é` (ci-ucp-invariance) agrees (the control); `(?i)[^é]` (ci-neg-fold) MISSES -- the whole subject folds to é, no non-é-fold character is present
field/hit `(?i)москва` (ci-moskva): all-uppercase Cyrillic folds to the pattern
field/hit `(?i)αβγ` (ci-greek-run): all-uppercase Greek folds to the pattern
field/hit `(?i)k` (ci-kelvin): the fold CLOSURE reaching outside the written range -- U+212A KELVIN SIGN, a 3-byte character, folds to ASCII k
field/hit `(?i)s` (ci-long-s): U+017F LATIN SMALL LETTER LONG S, a 2-byte character, folds to ASCII s
field/hit `(?i)[a-z]+` (ci-class-range): uppercase ASCII folding into the written lowercase range
field/hit `(?i)[^é]` (ci-neg-fold): an ASCII 'x' beside the fold-target É -- 'x' is NOT in the é fold class, so the negation matches it
field/hit `(?i)straße` (ci-strasse): the exact literal, lowercase
field/near-miss `(?i)straße` (ci-strasse): the all-caps 'SS' spelling -- 10.46 does SIMPLE folding only, no one-to-many foldings, so this must NOT match
field/hit `(?i)σ` (ci-sigma): a word carrying the FINAL SIGMA form (ς), which folds with σ/Σ under simple folding
field/hit `(?i)σ` (ci-sigma): an all-caps Greek word carrying Σ
field/miss `(?i)i` (ci-turkish-i): U+0130 LATIN CAPITAL I WITH DOT ABOVE -- locale-free simple folding does NOT fold this to ASCII i/I
field/miss `(?i)i` (ci-turkish-i): U+0131 LATIN SMALL LETTER DOTLESS I -- same simple-folding exclusion, the lowercase member of the pair
field/hit `(?i)abc` (ci-ascii-control): the pure-ASCII fold, the cheapest member of the family
field/miss `(?i)abc` (ci-ascii-control): pure ASCII with no 'abc' substring anywhere, in any case
field/hit `日本|日曜|日付` (alt-shared-char): the first branch, sharing the whole first character with the other two
field/miss `日本語|日本国` (alt-nearmiss): shares six of nine bytes with both branches, matches neither
field/hit `α|β|γ` (alt-shared-lead): the middle branch, all three sharing one lead byte (0xCE)
field/hit `日本|Москва|café` (alt-distinct-lead): the third branch, three distinct lead-byte groups
field/hit `a|é|日|😀` (alt-mixed-width): the 1-byte branch
field/hit `a|é|日|😀` (alt-mixed-width): the 2-byte branch
field/hit `a|é|日|😀` (alt-mixed-width): the 3-byte branch
field/hit `a|é|日|😀` (alt-mixed-width): the 4-byte branch

field/hit alt-cyr-64 (the 64-branch Cyrillic alternation, utf8_set_v1.md 5(d)): a common word ('дом', house) -- U4 COORDINATION: assumes the 64-word list includes this word; correct this subject if it does not
field/miss alt-cyr-64: an uncommon compound word unlikely to be among the 64 chosen branches -- U4 COORDINATION, same caveat as alt-cyr64-hit
field/hit `é+` (qnt-plus-2b) AND `é+?` (qnt-lazy-2b): three repeats of the 2-byte character
field/hit `(?:日本){2,}` (qnt-counted-3b): two repeats of the two-character group
field/hit `😀{2,4}` (qnt-bounded-4b): three repeats of the 4-byte character
field/hit `.{3,8}` (qnt-dot-bounded): six CJK CHARACTERS (18 bytes) -- within the CHARACTER bound despite exceeding it in bytes
field/hit `[\x{400}-\x{4FF}]{4,16}` (qnt-class-run): six characters, all in the Cyrillic block
field/hit `\bcat\b` (asr-b-ascii): a bounded word
field/miss `\bcat\b` (asr-b-ascii): 'cat' embedded with no boundary on either side
field/edge, the \b UCP PAIR: `\bМосква\b` ascii-scoped (asr-b-cyr) MISSES (Cyrillic letters are not ASCII word chars, so \b never fires); `(*UCP)\bМосква\b` (asr-b-cyr-ucp) HITS
field/hit `\bcat\b` (asr-b-ascii): the SAME bounded word beside multi-byte neighbours, confirming \b's ASCII scope is unaffected by adjacent non-ASCII content
field/hit `\B` (asr-B-midchar): two adjacent ASCII word characters -- \B fires at the ENGINE-invented non-boundary position between them
field/hit `(?<=é)x` (asr-lb-fixed) AND `(?<=a|é)x` (asr-lb-varwidth, the é branch): fixed CHARACTER width 1, BYTE width 2
field/miss `(?<=é)x` (asr-lb-fixed): a different preceding character
field/hit `(?<=a|é)x` (asr-lb-varwidth, the 'a' branch): BYTE width 1 at the same CHARACTER width as the é branch
field/hit `(?<!日)本` (asr-lb-neg): 本 preceded by 山, not 日
field/miss `(?<!日)本` (asr-lb-neg): 本 preceded by 日 -- the negative lookbehind fails there
field/hit `(?<=[\x{400}-\x{4FF}])\s` (asr-lb-class): a Cyrillic word ending the run, followed by a space
field/hit `(?m)^日` (asr-caret-ml): a second LINE beginning with 日
field/hit `(?m)語$` (asr-dollar-ml): the first line ENDS with 語
field/hit `\A日本語\z` (asr-a-z): the EXACT whole subject, true-start to true-end
field/miss `\A日本語\z` (asr-a-z): trailing content after the run breaks the true-end anchor
field/hit `\p{L}+` (prp-l): one letter from each of four scripts, cross-script
field/miss `\p{L}+` (prp-l): digits only, no letter present
field/hit `\p{Lu}` (prp-lu): an uppercase Latin-1 Supplement letter
field/miss `\p{Lu}` (prp-lu): lowercase only
field/hit `\p{N}+` (prp-n): non-ASCII digits -- the positive twin of cls-d-ascii's designed near-miss
field/hit `\P{L}+` (prp-notl): digits present (a non-letter run exists)
field/miss `\P{L}+` (prp-notl): letters only, no non-letter character anywhere
field/hit `\p{Zs}` (prp-zs): U+00A0 NO-BREAK SPACE, the positive twin of cls-s-nbsp's near-miss

field/edge `\p{Greek}` (prp-greek, Script | Script_Extensions) vs `\p{sc=Greek}` (prp-greek-sc, Script alone): Greek alpha carries U+0342 COMBINING GREEK PERISPOMENI, the stable Script_Extensions flipper this set authors AROUND U+00B7 (the confirmed version-sensitive point, utf8_set_v1.md 8.5/F-S1) -- both spellings HIT on the base letter; the oracle (U5) settles whether they diverge on the combining mark alone
field/hit `^\p{L}{4}$` (prp-l-anchored): exactly 4 letters
field/miss `^\p{L}{4}$` (prp-l-anchored): 3 letters, one short
field/hit `\p{Cyrillic}+` (prp-cyrillic): the strongest script filter in the set, two lead bytes
field/hit `\p{Han}+` (prp-han): pure kanji, no kana admixture
field/miss `\p{Han}+` (prp-han): pure katakana -- kana is NOT Han, so no run can match
field/hit `\p{Latin}+` (prp-latin): spans the ASCII / Latin-1-Supplement boundary in one property
field/hit the floor byte '~', per-call overhead control -- never inside a multi-byte sequence (0x7E cannot be a UTF-8 continuation or lead byte)
